Perean Ministry
puh-REE-an MIN-is-tree
noun phrase (a period of Christ's ministry)
From Perea (Greek Peraia, “the land beyond”), the region east of Jordan; the later phase of Christ's ministry conducted there and on the road toward Jerusalem.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Perean ministry is the name given to the later phase of our Lord's public work, conducted largely in Perea, the region beyond Jordan, after He withdrew from the hostility of Judea and before His final entry into Jerusalem. John records that He went away again beyond Jordan into the place where John at first baptized, and there He abode, and many believed on Him there—a fruitful season among people prepared by the Baptist's earlier preaching. Matthew marks the move: when Jesus had finished His Galilean teaching He departed and came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan, and great multitudes followed Him, and He healed them there. Luke frames the long journey of these months as a steadfast progress: He went through the cities and villages, teaching and journeying toward Jerusalem, His face set to the cross. Much of the richest teaching of the Gospels belongs to this period—many of the parables of Luke's travel narrative, the teaching on counting the cost, the lost sheep, coin, and son, the rich man and Lazarus, and the raising of Lazarus that hastened the final opposition. The dictionary marks the Perean ministry as a witness to the deliberateness of Christ's passion: He was not overtaken by events but ordered His own steps, ministering and teaching as He moved with set purpose toward the appointed hour at Jerusalem, the Shepherd going before His flock to lay down His life.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The later phase of Christ's ministry, conducted beyond Jordan in Perea and on the road toward Jerusalem (John 10:40-42; Matthew 19:1); a fruitful season of teaching marked by His deliberate progress toward the cross.

expand to see more

PEREAN MINISTRY, noun phrase. [Greek Peraia, “the land beyond.”] Christ's later ministry east of Jordan and toward Jerusalem.

He went beyond Jordan to where John first baptized, and many believed on Him (John 10:40-42).

He came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan, and healed the multitudes (Matthew 19:1).

Luke frames the season as a steadfast journey toward Jerusalem (Luke 13:22).

Much rich teaching belongs here, with His face set toward the cross.

📖 Key Scripture

Joh 10:40 — "And went away again beyond Jordan into the place where John at first baptized; and there he abode."

Joh 10:42 — "And many believed on him there."

Mt 19:1 — "And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee, and came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan;"

Lu 13:22 — "And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the danger is the critical fragmenting of the Gospels that denies any coherent ministry and the loss of Christ's deliberate march to the cross.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the deliberateness of Christ's passion. Some critical scholarship so fragments the Gospels into isolated units that it denies any coherent course to the Lord's ministry, treating the geographical and chronological frame as later editorial fiction. The dictionary affirms the Gospels' own ordering: the Lord withdrew beyond Jordan, ministered fruitfully there, and journeyed with set face toward Jerusalem and the cross. He was not the victim of circumstance but the willing Shepherd ordering His own steps.

The Perean season also recovers the breadth of Christ's teaching ministry. Far from a single dramatic act, His work unfolded over years and regions, and the months beyond Jordan gave the church some of its most precious parables—the lost sheep, the prodigal son, the rich man and Lazarus, the counting of the cost. The dictionary marks this against any reduction of Christ to a mere sacrifice without a ministry of teaching: He came to declare the kingdom and to die for it, and the road to Jerusalem was lined with the words of life as well as the shadow of the cross.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Perea (Greek Peraia, from peran, “beyond, across”), the region beyond Jordan; the phrase “beyond Jordan” recurs to mark the location of this ministry.

expand to see more

Peran, Greek, “beyond” or “across,” whence Peraia, the land beyond Jordan.

“Beyond Jordan” (Greek peran tou Iordanou) recurs in John and Matthew for the region.

The “place where John at first baptized” ties the season to the Baptist's earlier labours.

Luke's “journeying toward Jerusalem” frames the travel narrative of chapters 9 through 19.

The set “face toward Jerusalem” (Luke 9:51) marks the deliberate march to the cross.

Usage

"The teacher located the parable of the prodigal son in the Perean ministry, on the road toward Jerusalem."

"He showed that Christ ordered His own steps beyond Jordan, no victim of circumstance but the willing Shepherd."

"She marked how many believed beyond Jordan, fruit of seed the Baptist had sown years before."
